changelog:
Two additions: somewhere to see what you are running, and Plex.

**About**
- Settings now has an About section showing the version and build number, and a
  Check for updates you can press. Until now the app only looked for updates once
  at launch, at most every twelve hours, and said nothing when there was nothing
  new — so there was no way to ask.
- The check tells you what it found either way, including "you are on the latest
  version", and it ignores a version you previously said Later to.

**Plex — new, and not yet proven**
- Add a source has a Plex tab. Sign in through plex.tv in your browser; the app
  never sees your password, which also means an account that uses Google or Apple
  sign-in works normally.
- Your servers are listed with the connection the app would use. A server only
  reachable through Plex's relay is refused with the reason, because the relay is
  too slow for video and would look like a broken stream rather than a refusal.
- Choosing a server imports its films and shows, with episodes.
- **Playing a Plex item may not work yet.** This has never run against a real
  server — everything above was built and tested against stand-in responses. The
  catalog should be right; playback is the part most likely to fail, and it will
  fail as an error rather than quietly.

**Also**
- A Plex source is skipped by catalog refresh rather than being handed to the
  playlist parser, which would have reported it as an empty playlist.

Known limits: multi-view, picture-in-picture, DVR and recording are not in this
build. Catch-up still has not been tested against a real provider archive.
